registered_before: any X4 data; after the human residual by distance from foot events was seen (declared)

why.finding: human jumps (amendment-2 scope, registered estimator): 75% of frames above the state thresholds lie within 40 ms of a foot contact change (13% of frames); p99 within the window 0.64 BW, steady contact 0.06 BW, steady flight 0.31 BW; in walking the excess is not concentrated near events (0-40 ms 2.8%, 40-80 ms 1.7%, 80-160 ms 2.2%)
why.fairness: with one threshold (pooled p99, 0.24 BW) the human false-infeasible rate ranges from 0.0% (steady contact) to 9.0% (jump event window), so a motion with more take-offs and landings is penalised for measurement error alone; state-specific thresholds fix the human false-infeasible rate at 1% in every state
why.not_chosen: excluding event windows: hides take-off, landing and touchdown violations, uses the estimator's own event times, lets contact jitter remove most frames, and changes denominators

states.event: within window_ms of a change in either foot's contact (foot = heel or toe landmark in contact)
states.contact: outside the window, at least one foot in contact
states.flight: outside the window, no foot in contact

threshold.window_note: 40 ms primary, 80 ms sensitivity (约定，未经推演)
threshold.tau: per state, 99th percentile of per-frame residual over the kept human frames of that state, classes weighted equally; a class enters a state only with >= min_frames_per_class_state frames
threshold.min_frames_note: 约定，未经推演; set after the 17-frame whole-body flight class dominated the amendment-1 flight threshold
threshold.scope_and_exclusions: amendment 2 (no running, no yoga, ballet kept) and the amendment-1 exclusions
threshold.estimator: computed on the registered contact rule; recomputed with the estimator fixed by the X4 preregistration if that differs
threshold.envelope_variant: per state, the largest per-class 99th percentile (human false-infeasible <= 1% in every class and state); reported; choice between the equal-class-weight tau and the envelope open (pooled tau gives walking steady contact 3.8%)

x4_safeguards: report per method and arm the share of frames in each state
report infeasibility per state; the primary conclusion must also hold within the steady-contact state alone
direct standardisation: per-state infeasibility reweighted to a common state mix per task (mean over the compared arms; over methods for cross-method rankings)

contact-jitter flag: a run whose foot-event rate exceeds the human maximum (events_per_second_max_all) is flagged and, in a sensitivity analysis, judged with the steady-contact threshold on all frames
bracketing: three-state rule (primary), two-state contact/flight rule, steady-contact threshold on all frames; a direction is claimed only when all three agree
window width and threshold values frozen before X4 data; 80 ms window as sensitivity
limitation: thresholds come from marker-based human data with marker noise and soft-tissue motion that generated motions do not have; this can make them lenient for every generated motion alike, mainly affecting absolute infeasibility rather than within-method arm differences
